newsitem.title: IRAN: Quake kills five, injures 50 in northern Iran.
newsitem.headline: Quake kills five, injures 50 in northern Iran.

text.p: Several earthquakes hit northern and western Iran on Friday, one of them killing five people and injuring 50 near the border with Azerbaijan, Iranian media said.
An earthquake measuring 5.5 degrees on the Richter scale jolted areas outside Ardabil, a provincial capital 400 km (250 miles) northwest of Tehran, state-run Tehran radio said.
It killed five people, injured 50 and caused damage in most of the villages in the province, it said

The earthquake struck at 4.31 p.m. (1301 GMT), destroying many homes in villages in three districts in Ardabil province and shattering window panes in Ardabil city, which is near the Iran-Azerbaijan border, the radio said.
Three minutes earlier and some 350 km (220 miles) away, a quake also measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale hit the western city of Sanandaj, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage in Sanandaj, a Kurdish-populated provincial capital, it said.
Iran's northern province of Gilan on the Caspian Sea coast was also shaken by a tremor measuring about four on the Richter scale, but there was no damage, IRNA added.
Force four and five tremors are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in populated areas.
In early February, two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in northeastern Iran.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in Gilan and neighbouring Zanjan province in 1990.
